name: Frankleburg
tagline: The Land of a Thousand Queens
description:
# Frankleburg, the Land of a Thousand Queens
*Founded in 701-AF*

## Historical Overview
They say that there are one thousand queens in Frankleburg--- each with her own small queendom and culture. Roughly a thousand years ago the queendoms united to fight off their northern neighbor's aggressions. Initially, the treaties were for the sake of defeating the larger enemy to the north, (INSERT COUNTRY NAME HERE). But, even after the war, the union of Frankleburgian queendoms made them prosper. They were stronger together. Richer. Safer.

The original 1,000 queens signed the Grand Traité; also known as the Golden Treaty, and formally founded Frankleburg. One nation, united for trade, prosperity, and defense.

Today, the Queens of Frankleburg gather at the Ministry of Queens, where they vote on domestic and foreign affairs. While most Queens have their title via birth, in recent years a handful of them have been elected to the position by the peoples of their queendoms.

Perhaps due to its size, since its foundation, Frankleburg has been directly involved in very few wars. It is a large, and powerful nation. Rich in steel and gold. Frankleburg not only controls the second-largest navy in the world, but also one of the largest land armies.

## Cultural Overview
Frankleburgians pride themselves on being the great Creuset-- melting pot-- with a thousand different little cultures and peoples. Frankleburgians take great pride not only in their national identity, but also in their smaller, ancestral lineages.

""To be different is to be strong"" is a common motto in Frankleburg. Differences are celebrated. Those who shun others for those differences are, in turned, shunned. There are numerous legends about warm Frankleburgian hospitality. Being welcoming to all is an important point of their culture.

Frankleburg has a capitalistic economic structure, and is a constitutional monarchy.

It has no single religion, and is aggressive in maintaining a separation of church and state. Many of the western queendoms are of the Luminance faith, while their coastal regions worship The Fish. Many queendoms have niche, region-specific religious practices that are unique to their micro-culture.

## Racial and Magical Overview
With Frankleburg's aggressive focus on growth, prosperity, and the strength in differences, Franklebrug is one of the few countries who has taken the emergence of magic in stride. There is a race boiling away just under the surface. Every scholar wants to be the first one to unravel the world's magical mysteries.

However, Franklebrug remains largely hostile to vampires-- certain queendoms outright banning their participation. It is illegal for vampires to kill humans in Frankleburg, and feeding may only happen with explicit consent.

(Write blurbs for other species, TBD)

## Important Allies and Enemies
Relationships with neighbors TBD

## Important and Notable Landmarks/Places
### Capital: Cité D'or
The Capital of Frankleburg is Cité D'or, a neutral but very rich city that falls under no individual queen. Cité D'or is instead where the ministry gathers, and also serves as a domestic hub of trade, military training, and splendor. It was founded over several large gold vein deposits, and the city reflects that in roman-style architecture and lots of gold plating.

### The Queen's Library & University
Cité D'or is home to the largest public library in the world. It is the crown jewel of Frankleburgian collective knowledge and resources. It boasts in the ballpark of 200,000 manuscripts-- with dedicated librarians, scholars, and a robust filing system unlike anywhere else in the world.

An extension of the library is the University of Frankleburg. It is a huge academic organization, with a focus on free education for all. Any adults born and raised in Frankleburg may attend. Degrees are earned in courses that vary in duration from one to six years. Many of the world's foremost magical scholars are recent graduates of the University of Frankleburg.

### The Crown Pass
Frankleburg boasts a large mountain range, which protects their eastern boarder. The (NAME THE MONTAINS) mountains are incredibly dangerous, full of monsters, and nearly impossible to pass without a guide.

In 1555 the Ministry of Queens commanded the construction of the *Crown Pass*, which is one of the only ways to bypass the mountains safely. The road is paved, all the way to the peaks, and allows for cross-continental travel. It is also a great source of income for the Queendoms, as outsiders must pay a heavy toll to bypass its gates.

## A Random Fun Fact
Powdered wigs stuffed with flowers are currently a popular fashion trend.

name: Norus
tagline: Where storms guard the scholars' domain
description:
# Norus
*Founded in 675-AF*

**Historical Overview**
In the year 675 Norus was founded as a feudal kingdom of knights, lords, and ladies, but with a focus on patronage towards learning and self betterment through knowledge. In the year 944 however, a plague overtook the fertile countryside of the nation. As peasants died of this plague, they rose again as mindless and violent undead that would continue to attack, kill, and spread disease until their bodies degraded into nothing.

The loss of life from that plague led to a food chain collapse in the country. No longer were there enough peasants to farm the grain to feed the nobles to pay the scholars. The scholars traveled the world and found inspiration in the industrial revolution overtaking northern Vardoran. They turned their remaining population towards mining and steelwork as they erected vast machines to perform the labor of hundreds of men.

The century immediately following the great plague was riddled with smaller outbreaks of that disease, killing off much of the peasantry and nobility. The enlightened scholars somehow escaped most of the death.

The year 1050 marked the first year that more grain was being mechanically produced than was produced by hand. 1088 saw the creation of machines to conjure storms across the land to fertilize the fields and water the crops. By 1200 the vast majority of the farming in the country was done via automated means and the population dynamics had shifted to their modern state.

**Cultural Overview**
The people of Norus are now separated wholly from the means by which they feed themselves and create their worlds. Farming, mining, and most every other form of resource extraction and processing have been automated. A small crew of a dozen technicians handle the extraction of an entire mine. A single family can farm enough food to feed a thousand citizens.

The poor of Norus live in squalorous living conditions and cramped quarters. They easily purchase enough grain to survive and enough fabric to have basic clothes, but they have nothing to strive for and no hope to live for something of value unless they can break into the extravagant upper class, or if they can offer their lives for some other form of advancement. Opportunities for a better life are rare in Norus. The poor can't afford to pass them up.

The intelligentsia of Norus includes mostly descendents of the scholars and nobles. They are brilliant doctors, innovators, and inventors who make the most from their accursed land. The rest of the world thinks of these renowned scholars when they imagine Norus. Known for both their brilliance and their ruthlessness.

They rule the land via a string of cooperative alliances based around the hoarding and sequestering of knowledge. The more important the invention someone understands, the more power they wield politically. Therefore espionage and experimentation are the primary tools for political power plays in Norus.

Because most of the populated regions of the country are covered by constant clouds, storms, and rain, the people of Norus have a particularly unique approach to their worship of luminance. A clear day is a sign for celebration among the poor, a break from the gloom and depression of their daily lives. Norus' chapter of luminance focuses mostly on giving people the hope to live another day. It is most popular among the poor and joining the clergy does represent another way to leave the country. Still, many choose not to leave. After all, the people of Norus don't go hungry.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
The outbreak of magic and the birth of Mytts is bringing about hardship in Norus. The scholars have built their power on having all of the advantages. With a new school of learning, the playing field is being neutralized and it is severely threatening the balance of power. Mages of any variety easily wreak havoc on the machines, making insurgency and rebellion more common than ever before.

Who knows how Norus' society might dramatically change again with the adoption of magic into their automation? Maybe this could even be a tool to fight the plague. It's a time of social unrest in Norus. For some this is apocalyptic, but for others, it's a new beginning.

Non-human races are rare in Norus. Vampires of the land typically disguise themselves from the luminance. The well fed poor make for easy food for vampires who also don't mind the near-eternal storms. Werewolves of Norus often are quickly weeded out of society and are killed or banished to the wilds. Mytts represent a unique case. Some of them have found themselves treasured by certain scholars and also have earned the ire of competitors. Unlike humans, this new form of life does not have legal rights and protections, therefore they're subject to the protection they can acquire based on their skills in magic.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Relationships with neighbors pending. Should be near other Luminance worshipping countries.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**The Mountains.** Vushter is the largest permanent settlement nestled atop the steep peaks of Norus' mountains. Most refined ore comes here to be made into steel and to be made into machines for the rest of the country.

**The Fertile Valley.** Hollihavn sits in a high point in the fertile valley, the region of Norus that is truly always raining. The city features excellent drainage and sewage systems that were originally developed during the initial outbreak of the plague. Hollihavn was once the seat of the king, whose palace has since been converted into The Academy of Innovation. Hollihavn's streets are covered and breezeways between buildings are the expectation, particularly in the nicer areas of the city.

**The Northern Coast.** Halbjark is the port hub of Norus, and it represents the face the kingdom puts forward to the rest of the world. It is a port town where rare goods and luxuries are imported from across the world for the benefit of the learned few. Halbjark coincidentally is the seat of luminance's largest church in Norus. It's the place where Norus meets the world.

**A Random Fun Fact**
Because a core part of advancement in life in Norus is the achievement of a doctorate via a written thesis, many citizens are incredibly well educated on niche and useless subjects, even those who never finished their doctorates!

name: Novosvet
description:
# Novosvet
*The New Light*

**Historical Overview**
Seventeen distinct states make up the massive country of Novosvet. Until three-hundred years ago, these states were independent countries, kingdoms, and principalities. Arglia, the state in which the capital city Goldsteeple is located, was constantly torn by war due to its value in growing food. The sixteen countries of the region shared a common culture stretching back centuries, a culture of perseverance, pride, ruggedness, and a religious respect and fear of nature and war. However, the first Prophet Gabriel The Immaculate changed the direction of this land.

Gabriel claimed to have seen the light and understood its teachings. He came forth with a radical doctrine. He preached non-violence, love for one's neighbors, and understanding even in the face of pain. He lived by that doctrine. Gabriel built a small church in the middle of Arglia. Soldiers weary from war could stay there, so long as they agreed to non-violence on the holy ground. Various soldiers who were healed in that church learned to band together with their former enemies and became Gabriel's first disciples. They took new names and left into the land to preach of the light.

The most divisive tenet of Luminance was one that the kings would not stand for. Luminance preached that no man could hold dominion over another, and that all were equal under the light. The religion spread like an infection. The kings attempted to burn it out and uproot it, but their infighting kept them from unifying to squash the religion. A fringe religious group turned into a movement, and soon that movement turned into a rebellion. Kings sent armies to destroy Gabriel's church in Arglia, but by divine providence, none ever succeeded.

Gabriel died in the year 1000 AF. He did not live to see it, but his disciples brought forth peace. Upon Gabriel's headstone they built the foundations for their new capital. They declared the first disciple, Lucianus I The Resplendent, as head of the church of Luminance and they named their land The New Light, or Novosvet.

**Cultural Overview**
The church of Luminance rules the entirety of Novosvet. Although the religion predates the country, in modern times, they are culturally identical. The people of Novosvet venerate the light above all, and while they have no kings, the church does impose laws and tithe upon the people as a government might. But teachings that every citizen learns from a young age educate them about the tyranny of kings and the horrors of wars. The faithful understand the differences between their system and the horrible old ways.

Various Prophets have defined the culture of Novosvet over the centuries.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
Pending.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Vardoran's city of Brighthaven is governed by Solarus the Immaculate, and is a protectorate of Novosvet and The Church of Luminance.

Although geographically they are quite separate, Norus and Novosvet have repeatedly entered into proxy wars and trade wars. Novosvet needs grain, but they also can't publicly approve of Norus' claims to land. So smuggling food between the countries, across the continent, is an incredibly profitable activity.

Countries that do not worship Luminance are populated by heathens, who must convert. Until they see the light, no parley can be had.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**Goldsteeple.** The capital of Novosvet and the host of Luminance's holy head Lucianus IV The Resplendent. This city stands in a vast open field in the northern reaches of Novosvet. The massive church for which the city is named is visible for miles in clear weather, the tallest building in all of Novosvet, with its highest steeples capped with brilliant gold. The church itself is a city within a city made of layers upon layers of offices, chapels, meeting rooms, confessionals, and prayer chambers. A great brass bell sits atop the highest tower. Several monks are required to ring it and its sound echoes for miles, inviting all to worship the light.

**Dormiria.** The largest and most southern of the states, Dormiria receives little to no sunlight during the winter months. Their regional city is Auria, a city of lights. Even in the long night, light dances through the sky. The first Lightweaver, Zora the Luminary, hails from Auria, and her statue stands at the gates to the city. Auria sits on a rocky island in a frozen sea with only a single bridge connecting it to the rest of the land. In ancient times, it was believed that Dormiria would never be conquered due to its harsh winters and defensible stronghold. But the people of the city, led by Zora, delivered the head of their last king to the Prophet Nicholas and his entourage, allowing them to enter the city. It is said that the sun rose for the summer as Luminance came to Auria.

**The Docent Valley.** Western Novosvet sits at the southern end of the Hallowed Mountains. During the winter months, the valley is rocky, frozen, and treacherous, but during the thaw of spring, water from the mountains floods the valley, giving Novosvet a passage to the sea. The waters from the valley join the western continent's water system and eventually make their way to the sea. Its name comes from the Prophet Larz, who predicted its existence and discovered the valley's location during a legendary westward expedition.

**A Random Fun Fact**
Because Luminance teaches that men may not have dominion over land, Novosvet's maps label other countries as "regions" and use slightly different borders. They claim that the grounds of any church or the earth where worshippers of the light tread is Novosvet's sovereign territory.

name: Omen Plateau
tagline: Where the sun repels all but the hardened
description:
# Omen Plateau

**Historical Overview**
The Omen Plateau is an inhospitable desert biome with high mountains ringing it along one side that make the region difficult to enter or leave, much less cross the sunbaked and brier choked expanses that make up the region's interior. The region is characterized by blistering hot days and subzero nights. Originally settled by humans as refuge from vampire attacks with mixed results.

The human populations have their scant few cities cloistered around sheltered oases. The humans here have thrown off the oppression of vampires, having won a major conflict in the past and drove their enemies into the sun. While the land is largely infertile and bleak, it's these very same features that makes outside attacks incredibly unattractive. The absolute lack of natural cover against the sun makes for a particularly excellent vampire deterrent. The land is not particularly mineral rich, and its strongest strategic value is simply safe passage through to its neighbouring countries, being a broad enough region that going around is almost just as costly. Travel throughout the region is dictated through lighthouse towers, enormous towers that serve as guideposts across the distances. "Keep the tower at your back until you can see the one ahead of you." These serve as outposts for caravans and travelers and can have townships spring up around them outside of the cities. They are for the most part entirely under human control.

While they are not the dominant force any longer in the Omen Plateau, vampires continue to thrive in the region in a singular underground city deep in the wastelands beneath the Bramblescar. This spindly city spreads through sprawling underground tunnels and caves, where discreet nightkin might slip to the surface unnoticed.

**Cultural Overview**
Faith pending.

The denizens of the Plateau have fostered strong communal ties born of the harsh environment that quickly kills. Lone travelers are often regarded with curiosity, as the landscape all but necessitates working together. Travelling alone is usually the sign of either someone of incredible prowess or resources, or else a surviving victim of a tragedy. The foolish and unprepared who venture out alone almost never return.

The humans have a rich history regarding the usage of caravans. Both with historical pride in their roots first arriving here, and as a means of business. Moving trade goods between settlements as well as bringing them to and from distant lands. Maintaining the lighthouse towers is also seen as an honourable duty. They provide guidance to everyone moving through the region, as well as offering precious shelter. Control of these lighthouse towers however falls to the trade barons. Those that protect the people govern the people. And so there is not any capital city to be found, moreso there is a roving government that caravans between the settlements. Bringing goods and services, hearing grievances, and distributing justice. Brightly coloured and airy silks are the common dress for citizens. Anything to keep the sun and sand at bay. Gold and silver jewelry is also very popular.

On the flip side, the vampires of the region have cultivated a deeply reserved and almost ascetic lifestyle. Still feeling the pains of being overthrown, they have retreated to the only sanctuary they have left in the land. As such, they value the secrecy of their cavern home, and engage in limited raids above ground for precious sustenance. When even animal blood can be hard to come by without drawing the ire of the trade barons, blood becomes precious, and gorging habits of vampires found elsewhere in the world is looked down upon here. Their feeding habits are a low-hanging fruit for rude jokes from other vampire groups, but they are usually above retort, being master stoics with an uncanny degree of self control. Being indifferent to the cold nights, astronomy is a common and well versed pastime for the nightkin here, enjoying a vast cloudless sky to drink in. The banner of the vampires here is a black-on-white sun ringed in thorns.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
Trade is the lifeblood of the Omen Plateau, and so the denizens are rather open in terms of diplomacy with the other races of the world. They do however remain openly hostile against vampires, who had enslaved them in the past before they fought for their freedom.

Vampires of the region are cordial with other species, but remain tight-lipped about entry into the Zaladran, even to friends.

Schools of Illusion and Frost are the two most common practiced in the Omen Plateau. Heat shimmers and mirages for the day, and the subzero nights.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Pending based on final world map. They remain a thorn against the Parlour. The humans for being so openly anti-vampire, but being logistically problematic to attack. The vampires here are also an annoyance to the Parlour for their lack of hunger and ambition.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**The Lighthouse Towers.** Enormous towers that serve as guideposts across the distances. They are outposts for caravans and travelers and can have townships spring up around them.

**The Bramblescar.** A treacherous region of brier-choked wasteland. Beneath it lies the vampires' singular underground city.

**Zaladran.** The sprawling underground city of the vampires beneath the Bramblescar. Spreading through tunnels and caves where discreet nightkin might slip to the surface unnoticed.

**A Random Fun Fact**
The region is home to a dull-coloured vulture sub-species of harpies that love to harry travelers.

name: Pisciv Vol
tagline: The sea is their sanctuary, the ship their church
description:
# Pisciv Vol
*Founded in 105-AF*

**Historical Overview**
One of the oldest nations in the world, Pisciv Vol is a collection of islands that stretch along the shore of the continent. Once a series of disconnected tribes, they were united by their mutual faith of worshipping The Fish, and their deep hatred of the mainland.

In 90-AF their first Great Seer set out to unite the islands. She did so by 105-AF, formally naming the nation for their deity and the sea on which they rested. The Great Seers have been leaders ever since, chosen by a runic divination ceremony at birth and raised by their predecessor.

Pisciv Vol relies primarily on fish and trade, not possessing particularly fertile soil nor islands home to gems or precious metals. The people of Pisciv Vol are said to be more comfortable on ships than they are on land. Many of them live in sea-top towns on complex nets of ropework and flexible docks. They are the best seafarers in the world, offering valuable expertise to other nations. Shipwrights from Pisciv Vol are highly sought after, all retaining the long oral tradition of Pisciv ship making.

Their navy is one of the best in the world, and the largest by far. Most Piscivs own their own ship. Rich families upwards of a dozen. They learn to sail as soon as they can walk.

Few wars have been waged against Pisciv Vol. Frankleburg suffered a humiliating defeat in 1009-AF. As did Sul'uun in 509-AF.

**Cultural Overview**
Pisciv Vol is led by the Great Seer and a Council of Elders. However, the small islands function as largely independent communities unless there is a crisis. Island Elders oversee their own people, and only reach out to the Council if there is an issue. The Council gathers and meets once a season on Seer's Island, their capital, to address anything that may arise.

The people of Pisciv Vol are fervent worshipers of The Fish. Their livelihoods and continued survival depend on the sea. They offer bounty frequently. Boat-bound worship is a frequent sight. Altars of floating blue pyres are erected atop the ocean's surface to guide ships and burn offerings to The Fish.

They rely heavily on trade and a mix of nearby currencies. They do not have an officially minted coin of their own, but any silver and gold has value in Pisciv Vol.

Pisciv Vol does not formally condemn piracy. Some islands openly encourage piracy against the mainland. As such, piracy is very much present in the waters around Pisciv Vol. They do not target their countrymen, lest they incur the wrath of the Council, but everyone else is fair game.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
Pisciv Vol is 98% human. While there is a degree of mysticism, they are largely leery of magic. Magic is a gift from The Fish, and not meant for use by mere mortals. Its use is frowned upon, or outright ostracized in certain communities.

Talam and their brand of magic are welcome in Pisciv Vol, as they share a similar innate respect for the forces of nature.

Vampires, werewolves, and others are killed if discovered.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Pisciv Vol has a strong sense of national pride, and a long history of putting nations of the world to shame with their superior navy.

Frankleburg and Pisciv Vol have a long, complicated history dotted by war and naval skirmishes.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**Seer's Island.** The capital and largest city. Most of the island is city from shore to shore. It serves as a trade hub for the other islands, and 70% of the shoreline is comprised of docks.

**Princess's Crown.** A large volcano that is Pisciv Vol's southernmost island. The jagged peak looks like a crown, and is where the island gets its name. It erupts thrice annually, casting great plumes of ash and smoke into the sky. Worshippers of The Fish often dump bounties of the sea into the caldera as offerings.

**A Random Fun Fact**
Pisciv Vol does not sell shoes. Most sailors prefer to be barefoot or in woven sandals for the ease of climbing ropes or navigating slippery decks, so there is only one cobbler in the entire nation.

name: Qalidran
description:
# Qalidran, The Vampiric Parlor
*Founded 3-Post-Apotheosis (947-AF)*

**Historical Overview**
In the year 1-PA (968-AF) the Progenitor, the first vampire, descended into the mortal realm. In year 2-PA the Progenitor created his first three sirelings: the First Descendant, the Second Descendant, and the Third Descendant. The Three Descendants founded Qalidran on a remote peninsula in 2-PA (969-AF). They intended to create a country for vampires, by vampires, where they are the ruling and only social class.

The first three descendants created the world's first castle heart with their sire's assistance, and the first vampiric clan. They turned the worthy, powerful and resourceful humans who earned their way into their ranks with their prowess alone. Those without skill, without utility, would never be granted the gift of undeath.

Vampirism began to spread. Other bloodlines were born, some from the descendants' sirelings, others from curse or the land itself. Most flocked to Qalidran, as it offered blood, castle magics, and safe haven from the scourge of holy magic.

They gathered their forces, recruiting vampires to their cause. The Progenitor is their creator, their god, and their master.

Humans were gathered from the mainland, forced into farms to grow their own food and used to feed the droves of vampires that call Qalidran home. Their neighbors learned to fear them, and to fear the night. It is by night that Qalidran ships arrive on the shore to steal away those stupid enough not to hang garlic in their windows. It is by night they arrive to slaughter.

Nearby kingdoms grew tired of the threat they posed. 55-PA the peninsula was set under siege by worshipers of the Light. A coalition of many kingdoms set against them, the biggest army the world has ever seen.

The Fifth Descendant called upon the great wyrm of the sea, Sunderfin, a beast as long as the island is round, with teeth twice the height of a human man, to wrench Qalidran from the rest of the continent. The land gave way under the great wyrm's weight, sinking thousands of human soldiers, and separating Qalidran from the mainland. Today, it is an island nation with a rigorous hierarchy, permanent mist braziers, and a castle heart that sprawls the entire length of the nation.

**Cultural Overview**
Qalidran is both the name of the nation and its only city. It sits at the center of the island, made up of four regions: the Inner Palace, the Terrace, the Gardens, and the Slums.

The distance between a vampire and the Progenitor informs two things: their political power in Qalidran and their might as a vampire. The closer one is to the Progenitor, the more powerful their magic and the strain of their vampirism.

*Please note that player vampires may not be closer than 4th generation. There are at least three vampires between you and the Progenitor.*

Qalidran relies on barter systems. They trade for tools, fabric, and gold. Blood is given to all who call it home on a regular basis. The higher your social standing, the purer the blood you are supplied. However, even those at the lowest rungs of the social ladder never go hungry. Access to blood is considered a right, one guaranteed by the laws of the land.

Honor and social standing is everything in Qalidran. Crossing the wrong vampire may mean death for you and your clan. It is a complex hierarchy of vampires, as difficult as it is dangerous to navigate.

All of Qalidran is one castle heart, which other clans have been allowed to build their castles within. The size sigils are given is directly related to their population, utility, and military prowess. Clans who lose the favor of the Descendants will feel their walls closing in, quite literally. Those foolish enough to rebel will simply find themselves without a roof come the following morning. To cross the Descendants is to court Death.

Vampires of Qalidran are split into five major groups: The Parlor, The Temple, The Harvest, The Navy, and The Guard. Each of these groups are beneath the control of one of the Progenitor's Five Descendants. Their faces and names are not known. They rarely leave the inner palace and never do so without heavy guard.

**The Parlor.** The heart of Qalidran's political body. It is a tiered system, all serving the First Descendant. Every sigil may only have one of their members, usually their sigil leader, attend meetings. The Parlor meets within the Crimson Hall, a large room built in the outermost area of the Inner Palace, and is the only part of the Inner Palace that is accessible to those who do not live within it.

The High Table, which is located behind a screen, is made up of ten members, all of whom are believed to be second and third generation vampires of the Five Descendants. Their names and identities beyond their relationship to the Progenitor are shrouded in mystery. The First Descendant may veto or approve any matter that is brought to the Parlor without vote.

Beneath them is the Low Table, which is filled with primarily fourth and fifth generation vampires. Some vampires who are very wealthy, have large clans, or are uniquely powerful, may find themselves at the Low Table. The Low Table has 80 members. These members vote on matters that are presented to the Parlor. Should they tie, the High Table discusses the matter and makes the final decision.

Getting an invitation to the Low Table is a great honor. Clans engage in complicated political games to try and garner their seat. It is a source of betrayal, murder, and strife.

Beyond the Low Table is the Parlor's Congregation: a group of 120 people who are the heads of the rest of Qalidran's sigils. The Congregation is made up of vampires who lack power, are of small clans, or have little to no relation to the Progenitor. They do not get a vote, nor can they speak during Parlor gatherings, but they may bring written matters for the Parlor to discuss if they obtain the signatures of fifty clans. Members of the Congregation sit in long rows on bench seats below the Low Table.

There is a great deal of standing room around the outer ring of the room, between the Congregation seating and the walls. The public is able to watch Parlor proceedings, but they must remain silent or they will be punished.

Lesser criminals, those involved in robbery, fights, and the like, have their punishments decided by a jury composed of ten members of the Lower Table.

Major crimes, such as murder, unauthorized human contact, and terrorism, have their punishments decided by two members of the Upper Table.

**The Temple.** The spiritual body of Qalidran is under the domain of the High Priestess, the Second Descendant. She leads all major religious rituals. She is one of the only Descendants who is seen by the people at large. However, she hides her face behind a mask and stands with three other women who share her hair color and build. It is impossible to determine who is the Second Descendant, and who is merely a decoy.

The Temple worships the Progenitor. They believe the first vampire to be the source of all the vampiric magics, and all of the gifts that they enjoy as a result. Human sacrifice and ritual blood letting are common practices.

The Temple claims that the Progenitor is currently in torpor, replenishing his magics after giving the gift of new magic to vampires in 324-PA.

**The Harvest.** Members of the Harvest are the vampires who serve under the Third Descendant, and are those entrusted with the care of Qalidran's human residents. They ensure that humans are healthy and happy. After all, it is blood that thrums with life that is the most delicious.

The Harvesters are leaders in agriculture. They help their humans tend to their farms and livestock. They ensure that should one region face a difficult growing season, the other villages pick up their slack.

Many of the Harvest are also doctors and alchemists. Their primary duty is to ensure that the human population remains healthy. They respond quickly to any threat of disease or harm towards the humans. Members of the Harvest are the only vampires in Qalidran permitted into the human settlements, which are locked behind massive walls and fortified gates. It is a position that is only granted to those who have earned it.

The Harvest's other duty is to teach the humans within their settlements and find those with promise. Powerful mages or future brilliant scholars who may yet be worthy of the gift of vampirism. Only the truly excellent are offered a chance at unlife.

**The Navy.** Under the control of the Fourth Descendant, the Navy maintains Qalidran's borders. They ride great ships that carry mist braziers. The Fourth Descendant rides upon Sunderfin, the great wyrm. It is a large, undead sea serpent. It is the primary reason for Qalidran's supremacy at sea. Sunderfin can sink ships in a single attack, and is the reason why the waters around Qalidran never see human boats merely passing through.

Qalidran's marines are the few with permission to ferry vampires between Qalidran and the mainland. Boats only make the journey four times a year, and always under heavy guard. They also man all of the outposts along Qalidran's outer walls.

If disaster were to strike one of the human settlements on Qalidran, it is the navy who would go ashore on the mainland to replace the lost blood supply by any means necessary.

**The Guard.** Under the control of the Fifth Descendant, the Guard keeps the nation safe. They ensure that vampires follow the laws of the land, and keep any who are not related to the Descendants out of the Inner Palace.

All members of the Guard wear masks, referred to as Reds and Grays. Those with red masks reside in and around the inner palace. The Red Guard is made up entirely of those within three generations of the Progenitor.

Those from the fourth generation or farther out are members of the Gray Guard. Grays guard the large vampiric city that makes up the bulk of Qalidran, ensuring order and loyalty among the vampires who call the island home. Others are stationed at the outer walls, or protect the Parlor while it is in session. The unlucky few serve as guardians of The Fifth Hell, the prison that lies at the depths of the capital's sewers.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
85% to 90% of the world's vampires reside in Qalidran. Their vampiric population measures somewhere between 8,500 and 9,000. Their humans have flourished over the years, creating large coastal villages and communities. The number of humans on the island of Qalidran fluctuates around 100,000.

Qalidran has had mixed reactions to the emergence of the other magical races. Some view them as an opportunity for study and growth, while others discard them as useless for their lack of the vampiric magics. For now, their walls remain closed, but interested, in those who are not vampires.

Werewolves have been banned from the island after an entire village was slaughtered by one during a blood moon. Following the incident, newly acquired humans from the mainland are quarantined through their first full moon to ensure that no werewolves breach their human populations.

Qalidran's main city and capital is a single structure created out of the world's largest castle heart. Blood magic is plentiful within its walls, and is considered to be the superior strain of magic by most of its residents. However, most vampires have been quick to embrace the gift of new magic at their fingertips.

Giving the gift of vampirism is a big deal in Qalidran. Clans must put in a request to the Parlor to be given a human to turn. That human is selected for it from the human settlements. Only the best and brightest are given the opportunity to become a vampire. It is never their choice, however, and they simply go where they are told. To ensure that clans remain a controllable size, sigils within Qalidran are never larger than fifty in number.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Qalidran has no allies, only enemies. They consider non-Qalidran ships kill on sight and will sink anyone they find wandering in their waters regardless of the ship's size.

Specific information about coastal neighbors and histories between them pending.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**The Fifth Hell.** The largest prison that lies at the heart of Qalidran's capital. Many criminals are entombed in the walls, never to see the moonlight ever again. Vampires thrown into the Fifth Hell are left to starve as part of their punishment. Some perish due to starvation, while others waste away in their cells until their sentence ends. 70% of those thrown into The Fifth Hell never return to the surface. It is a maze-like structure built beneath the Terrace region of the city. It is full of traps, foul magic, and deadly pits. Rescue attempts end in death.

**The Inner Palace.** The home of the Progenitor and his Descendants. Those within three generations of the Progenitor all reside within the palace. If they leave it, they are accompanied by a great number of guards and always wear masks and veils. Only the Crimson Hall is accessible to the public. The rest is locked away behind tall walls and heavy gates.

**The Terrace.** Where most of the 80 members of the Lower Table reside. The largest and most powerful clans have been given the rights to build their homes within the Terrace district. The closer one resides to the Inner Palace, the more secure their position within Qalidran is.

**The Garden.** The bulk of the population lives in the Garden district, which is also the largest ring of the city. It is called as such because it is a collection of large homes that are separated by vegetation and trees. This is where the city grows vampiric plants, such as blood roses and thistle, as well as the lumber they need for construction. The large market squares, artisans, tailors, and blacksmiths are all set up within the Garden district. Everyone is free to wander here, and it is where 90% of the city's trade occurs.

**The Slums.** The outer ring of the city is the poorest area. This is the place for vampires without clans or access to the island's castle magics. They live in small hovels built by hand. Most are new arrivals, and the vast majority of the slum's residents will be adopted into clans once they have proven their worth. The Slums are the smallest district, filling the gaps between the Garden and the city's exterior walls. Some choose to live there with no intent of joining a clan. They are safe from the sun, the elements, and humans who want to kill them. They collect their septurn's ration of blood and keep to themselves.

**Human Settlements.** There are a dozen human settlements spread around Qalidran. One is in a walled section of the Terrace, while all of the others are outside of the city. Most of them are coastal, so their humans may fish for food, and also have space to grow the food they need to survive. Humans within the settlements rarely rebel. Their lives are worth more to their vampire keepers when the blood that flows through their veins is happy and healthy. They get food, healthcare, and are protected from external threats. To quell human rebellions, the elderly no longer have to give blood and may retire to die of a ripe old age. Humans between fifteen and sixty are expected to donate their blood once or twice a month. Their culture has twisted over the centuries, painting the outside world as something harsh and horrible. They believe that it is safest within their walls. The last human rebellion was in 213-PA. There have been none since. Humans who excel in might, magic, or smarts may be selected to become a vampire. After they have done so, they are forbidden from returning to their hometowns for the rest of their very long lives. They are also ineligible to join The Harvest for at least a century.

**A Random Fun Fact**
Qalidran is where most vampiric lingo originated, sigils, castle hearts, turn, tick, and more!

name: Sul'uun
tagline: By the Mercy of the Moon, by the Curse of the Sun
description:
# The Sul'uun Empire
*Founded in 112-AF*

**Historical Overview**
Sul'uun has a long, complicated history. A unification of tribes in 12-AF founded their kingdom in the heart of the forest of Uln. They enjoyed rapid expansion, plentiful harvests, and abundant rivers. In just a single century the Kingdom of Sul'uun became the largest country in the world.

At their onset, they worshiped a god of the sun. It was he who ensured their harvests were plentiful and their shores safe. It was to him that they pledged their loyalties. People of Sul'uun refer to him as the Great Sun, or the Holy Sun.

Their thirteenth king, and first emperor, was their undoing. Their greedy king turned his eyes beyond their borders, to the kingdom to their north, Lythe. Where Sul'uun worshiped the great and glorious Sun, Lythe worshiped the quiet splendor of the Moon. He fought long and hard to take over Lythe, but it was to no avail. He could not conquer their highland strongholds.

After years of war, the king of Lythe came to the thirteenth king with an offering. Join with his daughter in marriage, and lead both kingdoms together as Emperor and Empress of a new nation. He had but one condition. This newly founded empire was to worship the Moon. Not the Sun.

The greedy king agreed. He married the daughter of the moon and cast aside worship of the Sun. Sul'uun doubled in size, but their growth came at a cost that none were prepared to pay. The Empire of Sul'uun was founded in 334-AF, the first empire on their continent.

The Sun could not forgive their betrayal. Ever since that day, the Sun's rays have scorched the earth of Sul'uun. It is a land where rain never falls. The once plentiful forests are naught but a barren desert. Sand, red and burning, stretches as far as the eyes can see. Nothing grows in Sul'uun. The soil is unfit for life.

Now, the people of Sul'uun hide in their mountains to the north or the large, complex tunnels beneath the deadly sands. They beg the Sun to spare them, offering great tithes for mercy and forgiveness. The Sun does not listen.

**Cultural Overview**
Sul'uun is a nation focused on survival. While there is some desert vegetation they can eat, they rely largely on hunting wyrms, large sand-dwelling beasts that dwell within the earth, for food. They drink the creature's blood and viscera instead of water. They eat its guts and fashion its hard shells into tools.

Sul'uun imports large amounts of dirt and water to grow what food they can. Food is grown in large, hanging baskets. Should those baskets ever touch the ground the soil becomes corrupted by the Sun God's Curse and turns into red sand. Baskets of soil are carried miles across the desert, into the subterranean cities or mountain settlements. To drop vital soil and tarnish it is a crime punishable by death.

Sul'uunians have adopted several features of the great wyrms that they are forced to consume. Many have red or yellow eyes, and their skin has taken on a reddish or pink hue. They are a culture that believes in punishment, hard work, and a hearty heaping of a fear for the divine.

"It is by the Mercy of the Moon that we survive. It is in the Curse of the Sun that we burn."

The Empire of Sul'uun is unique in its worship, as they have a dual faith serving both the Sun and the Moon, the faith of Luntoll. There are ceremonies performed every day and every night to assuage the Sun's ire, and try to stay in the Moon's good graces. Common rituals are nightly prayer, group meditations, and collective dance.

The people of Sul'uun believe that the union of Lythe and Sul'uun represented a marriage between the Sun and the Moon. The Sun is referred to with masculine pronouns, while the Moon is distinctly feminine. Weddings are held at sunset or sunrise, when the divine couple shares the sky. Weddings held during the day or night are considered to be doomed at their onset.

To be caught worshipping another deity within Sul'uun is a crime. They believe that the Sun would take it as an insult, and heretics are executed immediately to ensure that the Sun does not punish their neighbors for their foolish transgressions.

**Racial and Magical Overview**
Mages able to assist in the production of food are elevated to nobility. Druidic and elemental mages are vital to the empire's continued survival. Sul'uun pays hefty coin to purchase mages from neighboring nations.

Vampires are exceptionally rare due to the unforgiving nature of the Sun. There are no trees to hide in, and scarce caves. While the cities are underground in large, man-made caverns, they do not take kindly to vampiric guests and would kill them upon discovery. A vampire would have to be exceptionally resourceful and skilled and more than a little lucky to traverse the sands alive.

Additional racial info pending.

**Important Allies and Enemies**
Pending based on final world map.

**Important and Notable Landmarks**
**The Sul'uun Desert.** The desert covers 95% of Sul'uun's territory. It is a harsh, unforgiving environment. The bugs are large, the days are scorching, and monsters prowl the sands for food at night. The sands are always shifting, with large mounds that are in a perpetual state of change. The sand is red. The color shifts to a more vibrant crimson the deeper one goes. The rocks beneath the ground are the same scarlet. Sul'uunians believe that all of Sul'uun is red, all the way down to the earth's heart. Luckily, Sul'uun is surrounded by mountains on all sides, so the desert has not spread beyond the peaks into the rest of the continent.

**Tolra, the Capital.** The capital of Sul'uun is located in the heart of the desert. The palace of the first emperor's tallest spires still pierce the sand that has buried the rest of the city. They serve as a beacon to travelers lost in the desert, as they are tall enough to be seen from several leagues away. As the city sank, so too did its people. Tolra rebuilt beneath the sands. It is a huge collection of caves and caverns, some natural and others carved by hand. People live in small houses carved into the walls, separated by sheer staircases and precarious paths. The hanging gardens feed the people, watered with freshwater that they pull from the depths of the earth. In contrast to the bitter desert winds, the city is almost always cool. Sul'uunians wear heavy carapace from the wyrms and thick, layered blankets to stay warm. The blankets are dyed in elaborate stripes of red, gold, and orange. The thin outer layer is worn while on the surface. The further down you go, the more layers you add.

**The Wana Crater.** The Wana Lake was once the largest freshwater lake on the continent. It was the Kingdom of Sul'uun's main source of water and fish. After the Curse of the Sun settled into the soil, the Wana Lake's water level fell and fell, until only a cracked crater remained. The Wana Crater is a stark reminder of the prosperity that they lost. Once a year, during the new year's ceremonies, faithful of Luntoll leave flowers, jewels, and other offerings at the crater's heart in the hopes that the new year will bring forgiveness and a return to the splendor they once knew.

**A Random Fun Fact**
Luntoll faithful execute heretics with sand burials, burying them alive in deep pits of red sand.
